title: Habitat fragmentation negatively affects effective gene flow via pollen, and male and female fitness in the dioecious tree, Spondias purpurea (Anacardiaceae)
notes: Same comparison measures visitation, fruit set, paternity/pollen flow, adult and seed/juvenile genetics.

title: Pollen flow and effects of population structure on selfing rates and female and male reproductive success in fragmented Magnolia stellata populations
notes: Six adjacent populations; paternity-derived pollen flow, selfing, female seed production and male reproductive success. Native model coefficients retained unless a compatible standardisation is locked.

title: Effects of population structure on pollen flow, clonality rates and reproductive success in fragmented Serapias lingua populations
notes: The source predefines anthropic C/F/G versus natural A/B/D/E/H/I populations. Primary site-level Hedges-g effects are reconstructed for C,F,G_adult; the -log(area) Fisher-z representation uses the same observations and is sensitivity only.

title: Gone with the wind: Negative genetic and progeny fitness consequences of habitat fragmentation in the wind pollinated dioecious tree Brosimum alicastrum
notes: Direct replicated habitat contrast; population/sex structure, pollen-distance gene flow, genetic diversity/mating and early progeny vigour.

title: Pollination and reproductive success across volcanic damage on Miyake-jima
notes: Natural disturbance/resource-loss anchor; exposure is volcanic damage rather than generic habitat fragmentation, so retain as secondary/moderator-sensitive candidate.

title: Pollen flow and next-generation genetics across volcanic damage on Miyake-jima
notes: Same study programme as PS005 but different campaign/year; never row-join as synchronized measurements.

title: Density-dependent pollinator activity and reproductive response in fragmented urban populations
notes: Local interaction-function chain; urban density gradient, not automatically a binary fragmentation contrast.

title: Contemporary pollen and seed dispersal in fragmented urban patch networks
notes: Same programme as PS007 but later parentage campaign; keep dependence/programme ID explicit.

title: Fragmentation, floral display, mating system and reproductive function
notes: Strictly self-incompatible; reproductive output linked to population size/floral display/isolation.

title: Adult genetic structure and historical habitat connectivity
notes: Adult genetic state represents historical connectivity; same programme but different temporal layer.

title: Contemporary offspring paternity and pollen flow across fragmented versus continuous habitat
notes: Contemporary inter-fragment pollen flow; all focal populations are remnant/fragmented, so treat as gradient/lag evidence rather than a clean binary contrast.

title: Consequences of habitat fragmentation on the reproductive success of two Tillandsia species with contrasting life history strategies
notes: Three-year plant-pollinator and female reproductive comparison; site nested within habitat in GLMM, so plant-level n is not fragmentation-level n.

title: Extensive Pollen Flow but Few Pollen Donors and High Reproductive Variance in an Extremely Fragmented Landscape
notes: Primary paper uses a highly fragmented landscape and compares some quantities to an earlier continuous population; do not treat as a clean same-study binary effect without reconstructing dependence.

title: Habitat edges decrease plant reproductive output in fragmented landscapes
notes: Experimental connectivity/edge design; flowering, pollination rate and seed production across five species. Strong candidate for D/I/F concordance tests.

title: Habitat fragmentation restricts insect pollinators and pollen quality in a threatened Proteaceae species
notes: Across 11 populations, visitation increased with floral display/connectivity; small isolated remnants lacked native bees and showed stronger pollen-quality limitation.

title: Small populations, big challenges: Genetic, demographic, and landscape context collectively shape population performance of a perennial herb
notes: Same study measures population size, SNP diversity, floral morph balance and reproductive performance across 33 populations; pollinator abundance in 15 populations. Small populations are genetically less diverse, while seed production is linked more directly to morph balance/pollinator abundance than to genetic diversity.
